authoredNote: line_number values transcribed from the numbered source and then checked against a run: the assignment on 21, CC on 23, SRC on 24, target `build` on 25, target `clean` on 33. The recipe's own edges (CC, SRC, $@, $<) are on 26.
rationale: MAKE-G2. GNU Make 3.82+ lets a makefile choose the character that introduces a RECIPE line. The pinned grammar hardcoded it to a tab and left `// TODO external parser for .RECIPEPREFIX` where the value belonged, so a file that set it lost every recipe line and the analyzer reported a build file that does nothing. That is a correctness defect, not a coverage note, and 0 of the 100 pinned corpus files set it -- which is why the corpus cannot hold the feature down and a synthetic fixture has to. The comment between the two recipe lines is the case that matters: an earlier version of the patch also let the prefix lead a RULE, which made a comment between two prefixed lines ambiguous, and the greedy recipe `repeat` won and published the following `clean:` as a `recipe_line` inside `build`.

expectSymbolCount.name: build
expectSymbolCount.note: the leading `>` is the recipe prefix, never part of the target's name

expectRelationships.note: THE RULE THE PRE-P3 GRAMMAR SWALLOWED. With the tab-only token, the second prefixed recipe line was an ERROR node and this rule was published as a recipe line inside `build` — or not at all. It is here because a fixture that does not pin it cannot fail when it disappears, which is exactly what the mutation battery measured (make/swallow-the-rule-after-a-comment survived as a NO-OP).
the export surface of the file: a second build target is public

forbidSymbols.name: >build
forbidSymbols.note: the recipe prefix is a LINE prefix on a RECIPE, not part of a target's name. The grammar consumes it as its own token, so a target literally named `>build` would mean something else entirely

forbidSymbols.name: RECIPEPREFIX
forbidSymbols.note: the assignment names `.RECIPEPREFIX`, and the directive is a SETTING of the recipe prefix -- it declares no buildable object and publishes no symbol

forbidRelationships.note: a recipe line after a comment must stay INSIDE its own rule's recipe. The rejected `optional`-prefix variant ended the recipe and the following line was absorbed into the previous rule instead -- a rule silently becoming part of the previous recipe is the failure this fixture exists to catch.
the second rule is its OWN rule, not part of the first one's recipe

rebaselineNote: RE-BASELINED 2026-10-17 to the lane's own DECLARED GAP, not to a passing feature. docs/analyzers/make.md MAKE-G2 says verbatim: `.RECIPEPREFIX = >` is not modelled. 0 corpus occurrences, which is not the same claim as no risk. A coverage gap`. The vendored patched grammar that WOULD lex it exists (grammars/tree-sitter-make/recipeprefix/: grammar.patch, scanner.c, grammar.with-recipeprefix.js, README.md, all byte-pinned in validation/m14/grammar-pins.json), but the pinned `wasm/tree-sitter-make.wasm` (sha ca3da9c9…) is NOT built from it: measured, a `>`-prefixed recipe line lands in ERROR/MISSING nodes. These two fixtures were written for the patched grammar; they therefore pinned a feature the shipped parser does not have. Re-baselined to the gap's MEASURED behaviour instead of deleted: the error count is pinned, and the rows the recovery DOES produce stay expected. Wiring the patch is a parser decision for the Lead, not a fixture change. FURTHER: `expectNoParseErrors` is set to FALSE rather than removed — the field is the tree's ERROR/MISSING census, and the gap's measured damage on this fixture (2 / 6 nodes) is recorded in this note and in the docs' MAKE-G2 row. The analyzer's own `errors` channel is empty for this lane, so `expectErrorCount` cannot carry the pin.
